TITLE: Unlocking the Potential of SMEs for Sustainable Development

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Unlocking the Potential of SMEs for Sustainable Development

HIGHTLIGHTS

Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) play a vital role in achieving the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) owning to their significant contributions to economic growth, job creation, and innovation.
Circular Economy practices can help SMEs contribute to sustainability by reducing waste and resource consumption while optimising the use of existing resources.
A closed-loop supply chain approach can improve both economic and environmental performance by focusing on areas such as design, procurement, production, distribution, usage, and reverse logistics.
Policymakers have a crucial role in promoting circular economy practices for SMEs by providing policy measures, training programs, periodic sustainability audits, and financial support based on achieved targets.

April 24, 2023

Nuanpan Thamanovanish

Nuanpan Thamanovanish

The growing awareness of environmental issues and the need for sustainable development has spurred Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) to adopt innovative strategies that promote circularity and resource efficiency. However, integrating these innovative practices into SMEs’ business models can be intricate. There is thus a need for targeted policy instruments to encourage their widespread adoption.

Can supporting SMEs unlock the key to achieving the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals?

SMEs play a crucial role in driving economic growth, job creation, and innovation. To achieve the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), SMEs must actively participate in adopting sustainable practices and driving positive change. As the backbone of the economy, they account for a significant share of businesses and employment opportunities. According to the World Bank, SMEs constitute around 90% of all businesses and create 50% of all jobs worldwide.
Despite their substantial contributions, SMEs often face unique challenges in adopting sustainable practices, such as limited resources and expertise as well as government support. It is therefore essential to support and empower SMEs in their transition towards more environmentally friendly and socially responsible business models, which will not only benefit their bottom line but also contribute to the broader global sustainability agenda.

How can SMEs contribute to sustainability and how to support them?

The adoption of circular economy practices contributes to sustainability. The practices provide a framework for SMEs to re-evaluate their business models, focusing on reducing waste and resource consumption while optimising the use of existing resources.
According to the research on the adoption of circular economy practices in European SMEs (Dey, P.K. et al., 2022), SMEs can significantly support sustainability initiatives by implementing a closed-loop supply chain focusing on vital areas of action which include design, procurement, production, distribution, usage, and reverse logistics.
The closed-loop supply chain approach shows to have a positive correlation with economic performance as it enables businesses to reduce costs associated with raw materials, waste disposal, and compliance with environmental regulations. These practices help to enhance environmental performance by increasing energy and resource efficiency, as well as minimising waste.
Furthermore, the design function of a closed-loop supply chain is found to contribute positively to circular economy adoption and higher sustainability performance, but other areas such as procurement, production, distribution, usage, and reverse logistics need better alignment with the principles of the circular economy.

Proposed measures include adopting a green supply chain strategy, ISO accreditations, support systems to help SMEs choose appropriate logistics, available information related to operations, repair, and recycling, as well as innovation to improve reserve logistics to control the flow of goods from their end destination back to their point of origin to capture value or ensure proper disposal.

What is the role of policymakers in promoting circular economy practices for SMEs?

In order to better facilitate the adoption of a circular economy, policymakers have an important role to play in creating a conducive environment for SMEs. Policymakers can support SMEs by providing policy measures to support and regulate through incentives and penalties, training programs to create awareness among suppliers, distributors, and consumers, periodic sustainability audits to help SMEs achieve targets, as well as financial support based on the achieved targets.
Successful implementation of circular economy practices requires a collaborative effort between SMEs, consumers, suppliers, and policymakers. This approach ensures that all stakeholders are aware of the benefits of circular economy practices and committed to the implementation.

https://www.worldbank.org/en/topic/smefinance
Dey, P.K., Malesios, C., Chowdhury, S., Saha, K., Budhwar, P., & De, D. (2022). Adoption of circular economy practices in small and medium-sized enterprises: Evidence from Europe. International Journal of Production Economics.

TITLE: The Africa Institute Senior and Postdoctoral Fellowships 2027 in UAE: Applications Now Open for Researchers in African and African Diaspora Studies

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Applications are now open for the 2027 Research Fellowships Program at The Africa Institute, Global Studies University, offering senior and postdoctoral scholars an opportunity to undertake full-time research residencies in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

The fellowship program is designed for scholars whose research engages substantially with Africa and the African diaspora, particularly across the humanities and social sciences. The 2027 call includes four named fellowships covering African diaspora literature, global African studies, visual and performance studies, critical humanities, gender, feminism, social sciences, and cultural studies.

The program brings researchers into The Africa Institute’s scholarly community, where they can advance major research projects while participating in an interdisciplinary academic environment focused on Africa and its global diasporas. The Institute is part of Global Studies University and describes itself as an international center dedicated to research, documentation, study, and teaching relating to Africa and its diaspora.

The application deadline is September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Gulf Standard Time (GST).

About The Africa Institute

The Africa Institute is based in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, and operates within Global Studies University. Its academic work focuses on expanding research, teaching, documentation, and intellectual exchange concerning Africa and African diaspora communities.

Its broader academic environment includes postgraduate education as well as research activity in the humanities and social sciences. The university currently offers graduate-level study connected to Global African Studies and Global Studies, while the Institute hosts senior and postdoctoral researchers working across diverse interdisciplinary areas.

The Research Fellowships Program therefore goes beyond simply providing researchers with time to work independently. Fellows become part of an established scholarly environment in which research on Africa and its diaspora is examined through historical, cultural, literary, artistic, political, social, and interdisciplinary perspectives.

The Four Research Fellowships Available for 2027

The 2027 Research Fellowships Program consists of two Senior Fellowships and two Postdoctoral Fellowships.

1. Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship in African Diaspora Literature and Cultural Studies

Named in honor of the celebrated author and Nobel Prize laureate Toni Morrison, this fellowship focuses particularly on areas connected with African diaspora literature, culture, cultural studies, and related intellectual fields.

The opportunity is intended for established scholars, including academics at the associate professor or full professor level and comparable scholars working outside conventional university positions. Independent authors and public intellectuals whose work has received significant recognition in relevant fields may also fall within the intended applicant profile.

Research should have a meaningful relationship with Africa, the African diaspora, culture, literature, or closely connected fields.

The Toni Morrison Senior Fellowship is a full-time, one-year residency in Sharjah.

2. Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship in Global African Studies

The Ali A. Mazrui Senior Fellowship honors the distinguished African studies scholar Professor Ali A. Mazrui.

It is intended for established researchers whose scholarship focuses on African and African diaspora studies, particularly where these areas intersect with the humanities and social sciences.

Suitable applicants can include:

Associate professors

Full professors

Scholars holding equivalent senior academic positions

Independent scholars

Recognized authors

Public intellectuals with significant work relating to Africa or the African diaspora

Like the Toni Morrison Fellowship, this is a full-time, one-year residency based in Sharjah, UAE.

Postdoctoral Opportunities

For early-career researchers, the program contains two specialized postdoctoral fellowships.

3. Okwui Enwezor Postdoctoral Fellowship in Visual Culture, Performance Studies, and Critical Humanities

The Okwui Enwezor Postdoctoral Fellowship is named after the influential scholar, curator, art critic, and intellectual Okwui Enwezor.

It is designed for emerging scholars whose work engages areas such as:

Visual culture

Visual studies

Performance studies

Art history

Art criticism

Cultural studies

Critical humanities

Related interdisciplinary fields

The applicant’s proposed work should connect meaningfully with Africa or the African diaspora.

Applicants for this postdoctoral fellowship must hold a Ph.D. awarded within the last five years prior to taking up the fellowship.

Unlike the senior fellowships, the postdoctoral fellowship is structured as a two-year, full-time residency in Sharjah.

4. Fatema Mernissi Postdoctoral Fellowship in Social and Cultural Studies

The Fatema Mernissi Postdoctoral Fellowship honors the prominent Moroccan sociologist and scholar Fatema Mernissi, whose scholarship addressed major questions involving gender, feminism, Islam, society, culture, and sociopolitical transformation.

The fellowship particularly targets emerging social-science scholars conducting research involving areas such as:

Gender studies

Feminist studies

Cultural studies

Social sciences

Visual cultures

African studies

African diaspora studies

The proposed research should intersect substantially with Africa and/or African diaspora studies.

Applicants must also have received their Ph.D. within the required five-year postdoctoral eligibility window before assuming the fellowship.

Fellowship Location and Duration

All four opportunities are full-time residential fellowships in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

For the 2027 cohort:

Senior Fellowships

Residency period: September 2027 to June 2028

Duration: One academic year

Postdoctoral Fellowships

Residency period: September 2027 to June 2029

Duration: Two academic years

Selected fellows are expected to arrive in Sharjah around mid-August 2027, ahead of the formal September start, so residency and housing arrangements can be completed before the program begins.

This residency requirement is particularly important for applicants to consider because the opportunity is not advertised as a remote or short-term research award.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The program is particularly relevant to researchers developing substantive academic projects concerning Africa, Africans, African societies, African cultures, and African diaspora communities.

Depending on the specific fellowship, appropriate disciplinary backgrounds may include literature, history, art history, cultural studies, sociology, anthropology, gender studies, feminist studies, performance studies, visual studies, critical humanities and other areas of the humanities and social sciences.

Applicants should carefully select the fellowship whose intellectual focus most closely corresponds to their proposed research rather than treating all four fellowship tracks as interchangeable.

Application Requirements

Candidates applying for the 2027 Research Fellowships Program need to prepare a substantial research-focused application.

The official application requirements include:

Research Abstract

Applicants must submit an abstract of up to 300 words explaining the research project they intend to pursue during the fellowship.

Project Statement

A detailed project statement of approximately 1,000–2,000 words is required.

It should explain the project’s research objectives, methodology or approach, and broader scholarly importance.

Applicants may additionally provide a one-page bibliography containing important sources relevant to the proposed project.

Two Writing Samples

Two examples of the applicant’s academic or intellectual writing must be included. These may be either published or unpublished works.

Letter of Interest

Applicants are required to provide a letter explaining their interest in the fellowship and proposed research.

Curriculum Vitae

An up-to-date CV outlining the applicant’s education, research experience, publications, academic appointments, professional experience, and other relevant achievements should be submitted.

Three Referees

Applicants must provide the contact information of three referees. The Institute will contact the referees directly regarding reference letters.

How Applications Are Evaluated

Applications will be reviewed by faculty at Global Studies University.

According to the official fellowship information, selection is based particularly on two considerations:

The quality of the research proposal

The applicant’s demonstrated ability to successfully complete the proposed project

This means applicants should devote considerable attention to the intellectual coherence, originality, feasibility, methodology, and contribution of their research proposal.

A strong academic background by itself may not be enough if the proposed project lacks a clear connection to the intellectual scope of the fellowship.

How to Apply

Applications must be completed using the official online application portal.

Applicants beginning an application should select the new-applicant option on the fellowship website, while applicants who have already started their submission can return to the portal and continue their existing application.

Applicants should note the following submission rules:

Applications must be submitted online.

Applications sent by email will not be accepted.

Late applications will not be considered.

Incomplete applications will not be considered.

All required documents must be uploaded through the application system.

Each uploaded file must not exceed 3 MB.

Applicants can access the portal to follow the status of their application during the review process.

Questions and technical issues relating to applications may be directed to applications@theafricainstitute.org.

Important Dates for the 2027 Fellowship Cycle

Applicants should take note of the following schedule:

Applications opened: July 6, 2026

Application deadline: September 30, 2026

Deadline time: 11:59 PM Gulf Standard Time

Application review and shortlisting: October 2026

Interviews: Expected around mid-November 2026

Offer notifications: Expected by mid-December 2026

Arrival in Sharjah: Mid-August 2027

Fellowship program begins: September 2027

Senior fellowships conclude: June 2028

Postdoctoral fellowships conclude: June 2029

The Institute notes that this schedule is indicative and may be adjusted.

Is The Africa Institute Fellowship Fully Funded?

Applicants should exercise caution regarding descriptions of the program as “fully funded.”

The official 2027 fellowship webpage confirms that these are full-time residential fellowships and refers to residency and housing arrangements, but it does not currently publish a fellowship salary, stipend amount, research allowance, airfare entitlement, health-insurance benefit, or detailed financial package.

Accordingly, prospective applicants should not assume a particular monetary award unless The Africa Institute provides further information through the application portal, an offer letter, or direct correspondence.

The absence of a published amount should not be interpreted as meaning that no financial support exists; it simply means that the exact financial terms cannot presently be confirmed from the public 2027 call.

Why This Fellowship May Be Important for Researchers

The Africa Institute’s fellowship program provides an unusually concentrated environment for scholarship centered on Africa and its diaspora.

Current and previous cohorts demonstrate the program’s interdisciplinary character, with scholars conducting research across a range of African and diaspora-related fields. The Institute currently hosts both senior and postdoctoral fellows under the named fellowship programs, reinforcing the program’s role as an ongoing research initiative rather than a one-time funding call.

For emerging postdoctoral scholars, the two-year duration can provide significant time for developing an ambitious research project. For established academics and intellectuals, the senior fellowships provide an academic-year residency devoted to research and scholarly engagement.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants should begin by identifying exactly which named fellowship corresponds to their research.

A competitive proposal should clearly establish:

What research question or problem the project addresses

Why the subject matters academically

How the project contributes to scholarship concerning Africa or its diaspora

Which disciplinary or interdisciplinary conversations the project engages

What research methods or analytical approaches will be employed

What the applicant expects to accomplish during the fellowship

Why the proposed work is feasible within the fellowship period

How the applicant’s previous scholarship demonstrates the capacity to complete the project

Candidates should also ensure consistency among their abstract, project statement, CV, letter of interest, and writing samples.

The application should present a coherent scholarly profile rather than treating each document as an unrelated requirement.

Application Deadline

The final deadline for the 2027 The Africa Institute Research Fellowships Program is Wednesday, September 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Gulf Standard Time.

Since incomplete or late submissions are not considered, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to upload their materials.

Click HERE, to apply.

Conclusion

The 2027 The Africa Institute Senior and Postdoctoral Fellowships provide an important research opportunity for established and emerging scholars whose work addresses Africa and the African diaspora across the humanities and social sciences.

With four specialized fellowship tracks, applicants can pursue projects ranging from African diaspora literature and global African studies to visual culture, performance, gender, feminism, and social and cultural studies.

The senior fellowships provide a one-year research residency from September 2027 to June 2028, while the postdoctoral fellowships provide a two-year residency extending through June 2029. Postdoctoral candidates must have obtained their Ph.D. within the required five-year period, while the senior awards are aimed at established scholars or equivalent recognized intellectuals.

Interested candidates should carefully review the requirements, prepare a focused research proposal, select the fellowship that most closely corresponds with their academic interests, and complete the online application before September 30, 2026.

TITLE: Workshop on Leadership, Governance, Resource Mobilisation and Digital Transformation of HEIs in Africa

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Date: 5th February – 8th February 2024 | Workshop Duration: 4 Days | Venue: Kigali, Rwanda

Participants: Registrars, Enrollment Managers, Academic Advisors, Staff of the Registry, Examination Managers, Project Managers and Officers, Staff Responsible for Resource Development, Partnership & Policy Managers, and Planning Officers

Registration Link: https://forms.office.com/r/hmxXWK6u8h

Introduction

From time immemorial, a university has always been seen as a collegial organisation, governed and managed by a community of scholars. However, in the last few decades, the collegial governance and management system was dismantled in part because of forces of globalisation and the need for universities to become publicly accountable, not just to their governing bodies and internal stakeholders, but to broader society and donor agencies. This trend has revolutionized not only the operations of the University of the past but has also recreated a new university governance and management model. Universities are important institutions in the 21st century and are essential to the way that training and education are provided.

They play a crucial role in practice, policy, and public discourse in addition to offering knowledge, information, and evidence. The higher education environment is dynamic and for the last 20 years, global university rankings have been a major and growing factor in higher education around the world. There is still more work to be done, even though rankings may have encouraged some universities to raise their standards. To support quality and improvement in all universities, promote sector-wide planning pertinent to national and regional contexts, accommodate a more diverse ecosystem of differentiated universities, and uphold and strengthen universities’ mandates to serve the global common good, academics and university leaders must comprehend and contextualize university rankings. For universities, funding for postsecondary education is a constant challenge.

Examining the mobilization of financial resources for higher education systems is necessary, with an emphasis on two fundamental issues that must be addressed by all systems: what proportion of financial resources should be increased for higher education, and where will these funds originate? In addition, to be able to respond to societal needs, Africa’s higher education landscape requires visionary leadership, effective governance, sustainable resource mobilization, and seamless digital integration. Registrars are pivotal to maintaining the smooth functioning of the universities and play a key role in the above functions. Registrars typically serve as key administrative officers, overseeing various aspects related to student affairs, academic records, and institutional governance. Their responsibilities are diverse and essential for maintaining order and efficiency within the university. Their work schedule, roles, and responsibilities contribute significantly to the overall success and reputation of the institution. However, given the increasing complexity of the environment of HEIs, leading and managing such institutions requires unique and transformational leadership, management, and digital competencies, which some university managers are lacking. It is against this backdrop that the Association of African Universities (AAU) is organizing a capacity-building workshop for university registrars and administrators in universities.

General objective

The workshop aims to bring together key stakeholders, including academic leaders, registrars, and administrators, to deliberate on and concretise strategies for enhancing leadership, governance, resource mobilization, and digital transformation in Higher Education Institutions. This workshop seeks to empower participants with the knowledge and tools needed to lead transformative change in their respective institutions, fostering a collaborative and innovative higher education landscape in Africa.

Specific Objectives

Provide participants with a deep understanding of the key elements—leadership, governance, resource mobilization, and digital transformation—that shape the trajectory of HEIs in Africa.

Showcase successful models and best practices from institutions that have successfully navigated challenges and achieved transformative growth.

Equip participants with practical skills and strategies to lead and implement positive change within their respective institutions.

Engage participants on the importance, merits, and demerits of university ranking systems and context-specific application of ranking metrics and indicators

Facilitate networking opportunities for participants to engage in meaningful discussions, share experiences, and explore potential collaborations and partnerships.

Expected outcomes

The expected outcomes include:

Enhanced understanding of effective leadership, governance, resource mobilization, and digital transformation in the context of African HEIs.

Identification of actionable strategies and best practices for immediate implementation.

Networking opportunities for potential collaborations and partnerships.

Development of a collective commitment to drive positive change in African higher education.

Course Fee:

$950 per participant(excluding hotel accommodation)

Methodology

The workshop has adopted a strategic methodology that will include effective approaches, such as the use of case studies, focused group discussions, experiential learning (case studies from universities in various regions in Africa), presentations, and sharing of ideas, knowledge, and skills. The participants will have the opportunity to engage in dialogues with peers on the various challenges at their universities and map out strategies to overcome them.

Summary of the Course Content

Leadership in Higher Education

Define the characteristics of effective and transformational leadership in the context of HEIs.

Discuss the importance of fostering leadership skills among academic and administrative staff.

Develop Leadership Skills for HEI Professionals

Case Studies: Successful Leadership Models in the contexts of universities in Africa

Governance in Higher Education

Analyze the role of governance structures in ensuring accountability, transparency, and efficient decision-making.

Explore models of governance that align with the unique challenges and opportunities faced by African HEIs.

Best Practices Showcase: Governance Models from Successful HEIs

Resource mobilisation

Examine the current state of resource mobilization in African HEIs.

Understand Resource Mobilization Systems, the Donor Environment, Donor Characteristics and Expectations

Key Observations and Elements in Formulating Convincing Proposals for Resource Mobilization

Strategic Models for Sustainable Resource Mobilization

Discuss strategies for diversifying funding sources, including public-private-philanthropic partnerships, alumni engagement, and international collaborations.

Digital transformation

Assess the current level of digitalization in African HEIs and identify gaps.

Explore the role of e-learning, online platforms, and data analytics in improving the overall quality of education.

Critical steps needed to digitally transform HEIs in Africa

The confluence of Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity

Case Studies: Successful Integration of Technology in Education

About the Organization

The Association of African Universities (AAU) is an international non-governmental organisation set up by the universities in Africa to promote cooperation among them and between them and the international academic community. With over 400 members across the African continent, AAU is the largest and most comprehensive organization representing Universities and Higher Education bodies in Africa. It is also the apex organization and forum for consultation, exchange of information, and cooperation among institutions of higher education in Africa, and represents the voice of higher education in Africa on regional and international bodies ,and supports networking by institutions of higher education in teaching, research, information exchange, and dissemination. The AAU, with headquarters in Accra, Ghana, was founded in 1967, following recommendations made at an earlier conference organized by the United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) in Antananarivo, Madagascar in September 1962 for the formation of such an apex organization. The mission of the AAU is to raise the quality of higher education in Africa and strengthen its contribution to African development by fostering collaboration among its member institutions.

TITLE: AAU Launches Digital Empowerment MOOCs to Enhance Inclusivity in African HE

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
For Immediate Release

Accra, Ghana – (November 22, 2025) —

The Association of African Universities (AAU) is proud to announce the official launch of its Digital Empowerment Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) Initiative, a strategic intervention designed to propel the technological advancement of higher education across Africa.

The platform was unveiled by the AAU Secretary-General, Professor Olusola Oyewole, on November 14, 2025, during the closing ceremony of the Africa Universities’ Day celebrations. In his address, Professor Oyewole called for a fundamental shift in how universities harness technology, urging institutions to expand their digital capacity-building efforts beyond faculty and students to include administrators and all staff within the academic value chain. This initiative delivers on that vision by providing accessible, scalable, and high-quality training in three critical domains: (1) Cybersecurity Fundamentals for University Systems (2) AI Essentials for Teaching and Administration (3) Digital Literacy for Modern Academia

The initiative is designed to equip university staff across Africa with critical digital skills, strengthen institutional capacity, and enhance the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity practices in teaching, research, and administration. It forms part of AAU’s broader strategy to strengthen digital competencies among academic and administrative staff across its 450 member universities, supporting the African Union’s Agenda 2063 vision of a knowledge-driven, digitally empowered Africa.

The Digital Empowerment MOOCs will be delivered in a blended format, combining three-week self-paced online sessions with a day’s contact session (virtual) with facilitators, followed by an optional one-week in-person practical workshop to maximize participation and impact.

The first online cohort runs from from February 2 to 20, 2026. Registration for the online sessions is free and can be completed via https://forms.office.com/r/JLb6fkHWeF.

The in-person workshop will take place in April, 2026, at the AAU Secretariat, located on the Trinity Avenue, East Legon, Accra, Ghana It focuses on advanced strategic planning, leadership in digital transformation, and technology adoption. The workshop fee, USD 400, covers facilitation, materials, and meals. Payment can be made via https://pay.aau.org/digital-empowerment-moocs.

Participants will engage in video lectures, interactive simulations, case studies, discussion forums, and capstone projects, enabling practical application of acquired skills. The MOOCs initiative aims to deliver measurable benefits to staff and institutions across Africa, with at least 80% of participants expected to improve proficiency in digital, AI, and cybersecurity tools. It also aims to help institutions to reduce minor cybersecurity incidents by 50% while accelerating AI-driven processes within 12 months. Successful participants will be awarded certificates, enhancing professional visibility and institutional benchmarking.

The programme was designed with subject matter experts, strategic partners, university staff, and ICT directors to deliver practical and contextually relevant content. The AAU is, thus, by this release, inviting university administrators, teaching staff, ICT professionals, students, and sector partners to participate in this transformative initiative. We believe that by building a digitally empowered workforce, African universities will enhance innovation, strengthen operational resilience, and contribute meaningfully to Africa’s long-term development goals.

Please contact aaulms@aau.org for further information.

For Media Enquiries,

Dr. Felicia Nkrumah Kuagbedzi

Email: fnkrumah@aau.org

About the AAU

The Association of African Universities is an international, non-profit, non-governmental organization created by African universities to promote cooperation among institutions on the continent and strengthen their engagement with the global academic community. Founded in 1967, the AAU serves as the voice of higher education in Africa. Its mission is to enhance the quality, relevance, and sustainability of African higher education by supporting institutional development, fostering collaboration, and promoting innovation across the continent.

TITLE: Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028: Fully Funded Postdoctoral Fellowship at Harvard University

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028 is now accepting applications from outstanding early-career scholars who have recently completed, or are nearing completion of, a PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in the social sciences.

Hosted by the Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies at Harvard University, the Academy Scholars Program is a prestigious two-year, in-residence postdoctoral fellowship designed for researchers whose work combines strong social science scholarship with deep knowledge of countries or regions outside the United States and Canada.

The programme provides selected scholars with substantial financial support, research assistance, mentoring, access to Harvard’s academic community and dedicated time to develop ambitious research and publication projects. For the 2027–2028 cohort, the application deadline is September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

The Harvard Academy is highly selective. It receives more than 500 applications in many years and normally selects only five or six Academy Scholars for each cohort.

About the Harvard Academy Scholars Program

The Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies is housed within the Weatherhead Center for International Affairs at Harvard University.

Its mission is to promote innovative social science research while deepening understanding of the experiences and practices of different regions and countries around the world.

The Academy Scholars Program was established to support outstanding researchers at the beginning of their academic careers whose work combines:

Excellence in a social science discipline

Strong regional or country expertise

Knowledge of languages relevant to their research where appropriate

Original and innovative research

Comparative, transnational or domestic research questions

The potential to develop a successful career in a research university or international institution

The programme is particularly interested in scholars whose research connects disciplinary expertise with knowledge of regions outside the United States and Canada.

What Is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program?

The Academy Scholars Program is a two-year, in-residence postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Each year, approximately five to six scholars are selected for two-year appointments. Selected scholars receive an annual stipend of US$80,000, in addition to US$6,000 in annual research support.

The fellowship provides scholars with the time and resources necessary to undertake substantial research, writing and professional development during the early stages of their academic careers.

Academy Scholars become part of a select interdisciplinary community and participate in academic activities with other scholars and Harvard faculty members.

The programme also provides opportunities for scholars to interact with the Harvard Academy’s Senior Scholars, who serve as mentors and members of the selection committee.

Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028 Benefits

The fellowship provides several important benefits designed to support scholars during their two-year appointment.

1. Annual Stipend of US$80,000

Each Academy Scholar receives an annual stipend of US$80,000.

This substantial financial support allows fellows to dedicate significant time to research, writing and academic development without the financial pressures that can accompany early-career research.

2. Annual Research Support of US$6,000

In addition to the annual stipend, Academy Scholars receive US$6,000 per year in research support.

This funding can help facilitate research-related activities associated with the scholar’s approved academic work.

3. Two-Year Fellowship

The appointment is structured as a two-year postdoctoral fellowship.

The fellowship provides an extended period for scholars to develop their research programmes, publish academic work and establish themselves as independent researchers.

The Academy notes that the two years must be completed within a three-year window.

4. Research and Writing Opportunities

The programme is specifically designed to provide scholars with time to undertake significant research and writing.

Scholars may use the fellowship period to develop work based on their doctoral research, prepare a dissertation for publication or begin a new research project.

5. Mentorship

Academy Scholars are mentored by the Harvard Academy’s Senior Scholars.

These faculty members participate in Academy activities and support fellows as they develop their research and academic careers.

6. Interdisciplinary Academic Community

Academy Scholars participate in dinners, seminars and informal academic gatherings.

These activities encourage scholars from different disciplines and regional specializations to exchange ideas and develop interdisciplinary approaches to research.

7. Harvard University Research Environment

Being based at Harvard University provides Academy Scholars with access to a major international academic environment and opportunities to interact with researchers, faculty and other scholars.

The programme is particularly suited to researchers who would benefit from an intellectually intensive period dedicated to research and publication.

Who Is Eligible for the Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028?

The Academy Scholars Program is open to scholars from all countries and citizenships.

However, applicants must meet specific doctoral and disciplinary requirements.

The programme is intended for scholars who have recently completed or are nearing completion of a PhD or equivalent degree in the social sciences. Equivalent degrees include programmes such as the DPhil and SJD where applicable.

Applicants Who Have Already Completed Their PhD

If you have completed your PhD, your degree must have been completed within two years of the fellowship’s August 1, 2027 start date.

For the September 18, 2026 application deadline, applicants who have already completed their PhD must have completed it on or after August 1, 2025.

Current PhD Candidates

Applicants who are still completing their doctoral degree may also apply.

However, they must be sufficiently advanced in their programme and able to provide official degree-conferral documentation from their university registrar by June 30, 2027.

This requirement is important because successful applicants must be able to begin the fellowship on the required schedule.

Applicants Who Have Previously Held a Postdoctoral Fellowship

Individuals who hold or have completed another postdoctoral fellowship are not eligible to apply.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider their previous postdoctoral experience before submitting an application.

Eligible Fields of Study

The Harvard Academy does not accept applications from every academic discipline.

The programme focuses on the social sciences, particularly research that examines regions and countries outside the United States and Canada.

Applicants from regional studies disciplines may also be considered when their research is clearly grounded in one or more of the accepted social science disciplines.

Regional Studies Fields That May Be Eligible

A Major Requirement: Research Must Focus Outside the United States or Canada

Applicants should pay close attention to the Academy’s regional focus.

The programme seeks scholars whose work combines social science expertise with knowledge of countries or regions outside the United States or Canada.

Therefore, an otherwise eligible scholar may not qualify if the proposed research is primarily focused on the United States or Canada.

This regional requirement is central to the intellectual purpose of the programme and distinguishes the Academy Scholars Program from many other postdoctoral fellowships.

Harvard Academy Scholars Program Application Requirements

Applicants must submit a complete online application containing several important documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a CV that includes their academic and professional background as well as a list of publications.

The CV should provide a clear overview of the applicant’s:

Academic qualifications

Research experience

Publications

Awards and recognitions

Fellowships

Professional appointments

Relevant academic activities

2. Research Proposal

Applicants must submit a research proposal of no more than 2,000 words.

The proposal should explain the intellectual objectives of the research and the methodological and disciplinary work the applicant plans to undertake.

The Academy’s selection committee is particularly interested in:

The relevance of the proposed research

Its contribution to the applicant’s discipline

The originality of the research

The researcher’s plans for the two-year fellowship

Future publication plans

Future research plans

References and citations do not count toward the 2,000-word limit.

3. Scholarly Writing Sample

Applicants must submit one scholarly writing sample.

Examples include:

A peer-reviewed academic journal article

Another substantial scholarly work

The writing sample must:

Be written in English

Be no longer than 50 pages

Represent approximately the length of a single PhD dissertation chapter or academic journal article

Be submitted as one sample only

A published or unpublished work may be used.

Co-authored work is permitted provided that the applicant’s contribution is clearly identified and the work is not co-authored with an academic adviser.

4. PhD Program Transcript

Applicants must submit a copy of their PhD programme transcript.

For applicants who studied at universities outside the United States, the Academy advises that applicants provide as much official transcript-like documentation as their university registrar can provide for their graduate studies, including relevant Master’s and PhD records.

Where Is the Fellowship Located?

Residency and Fieldwork Requirements

Academy Scholars are expected to be in residence and participate fully in the scholarly community during the formal programming period, which runs approximately from late August through the end of April.

Scholars can conduct extensive fieldwork during the winter, spring and summer breaks.

Short trips for conferences and other academic engagements may be permitted provided that they do not interfere with Harvard Academy obligations.

This requirement is important for applicants whose research involves extensive international fieldwork.

The fellowship is designed around participation in an active academic community at Harvard rather than being a fully remote research fellowship.

Can the Fellowship Start Date Be Deferred?

No.

Successful applicants cannot postpone or defer the August 1, 2027 start date.

Year 1 must begin no later than the fall immediately following the fellowship offer.

The two fellowship years must also be completed within the programme’s specified three-year window.

Applicants should therefore apply only if they will be able to commit to the required timeline.

How Competitive Is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program?

The Academy Scholars Program is extremely competitive.

The Harvard Academy states that it receives more than 500 applications in many years but typically selects only five or six scholars.

Historical statistics demonstrate the selectivity of the programme. For example:

Fall 2016: 716 completed applications, 4 selected

Fall 2019: 585 completed applications, 5 selected

Fall 2022: 350 completed applications, 5 selected

Fall 2024: 533 completed applications, 6 selected

Fall 2025: 522 completed applications, 5 selected

These figures demonstrate why applicants need to present a highly focused research agenda and compelling evidence of scholarly potential.

How to Prepare a Strong Harvard Academy Application

Because the programme is highly selective, applicants should approach the application strategically.

1. Develop a Clear Research Question

Your research proposal should communicate exactly what problem you intend to investigate.

Avoid presenting a broad topic without a clear research question.

Explain:

What you want to study

Why the question matters

What is already known

What gap your research addresses

What contribution you intend to make

How you will conduct the research

2. Demonstrate Disciplinary Contribution

The Academy specifically emphasizes the relevance and contribution of the proposed research to the applicant’s discipline.

Your proposal should therefore make the academic contribution explicit rather than assuming that the committee will infer it.

3. Explain Your Two-Year Research Plan

Applicants should explain how they intend to use the fellowship period.

For example, a scholar may use the first year to develop doctoral research into a book or series of articles and use the second year to begin a new research project.

If you plan to move in a new research direction, explain how the new project connects with or expands upon your doctoral research.

4. Select Your Writing Sample Carefully

The writing sample is an important demonstration of your scholarly ability.

Choose one piece that clearly demonstrates:

Strong argumentation

Original thinking

Research competence

Evidence-based analysis

Clear academic writing

Strong methodological reasoning where relevant

Do not submit multiple writing samples because the Academy specifically requests only one.

5. Contact Recommenders Early

Since recommendation letters must be submitted separately, applicants should contact their recommenders well before the application deadline.

Waiting until the final days can create unnecessary risks, especially if a recommender is unavailable or encounters technical difficulties.

6. Check Your Regional Fit

One of the most important elements of the Academy Scholars Program is its focus on regions outside the United States and Canada.

Applicants should clearly demonstrate how their research engages with a specific country, region or broader comparative question that fits the Academy’s mission.

Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for Early-Career Researchers

The transition from completing a PhD to establishing an independent academic career can be challenging.

Researchers often need time to transform doctoral research into publications while developing new research projects and establishing an independent scholarly identity.

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program addresses this need by providing:

A two-year research environment

A substantial annual stipend

Dedicated research funding

Mentorship

An interdisciplinary scholarly community

Opportunities for academic exchange

Time to develop publications

Access to the Harvard academic environment

The programme is particularly valuable for researchers whose work sits at the intersection of social science discipline and regional expertise.

However, applicants studying outside the United States should ensure that their academic documentation is sufficiently detailed.

The Academy advises international applicants to obtain official transcript-like documentation for their graduate studies from their university registrar where necessary.

Applicants should also consider the practical implications of an in-residence fellowship in Cambridge, Massachusetts, including the requirement to participate in the programme’s formal activities.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program may be particularly suitable for an applicant who:

Has recently completed a PhD in an eligible social science field

Is an advanced doctoral candidate nearing completion

Has a strong academic record

Has a clearly defined research agenda

Conducts research focused on a region outside the United States or Canada

Has demonstrated scholarly potential

Has strong writing and research experience

Wants to develop doctoral research into publications

Is planning an independent research project

Can commit to a two-year in-residence fellowship

Has not previously completed a postdoctoral fellowship

Researchers from Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and other regions may apply because the programme accepts scholars of all nationalities, provided they satisfy the academic and research requirements.

How to Apply for the Harvard Academy Scholars Program

Applications are submitted online through the Harvard Academy’s application system.

Applicants should prepare the required documents before beginning the submission process:

Curriculum vitae with publication list

Research proposal of no more than 2,000 words

One English-language scholarly writing sample of no more than 50 pages

PhD programme transcript

Three confidential letters of recommendation

All application materials are submitted online as PDF documents.

The application should be completed and submitted by September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT, while recommendation letters must arrive by September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Applicants can access the application through the official Harvard Academy website.

Official Harvard Academy Scholars Program:

Visit the Harvard Academy Scholars Program page

Online Application:

Apply through Harvard’s online application portal

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Harvard Academy Scholars Program fully funded?

The programme provides substantial financial support, including an annual US$80,000 stipend and US$6,000 annual research support. It is therefore a highly funded postdoctoral fellowship, although applicants should review the official terms carefully rather than assuming that every possible personal expense is covered.

Can applicants from Africa apply?

Yes. The Academy states that the programme is open to scholars from all countries and citizenships. African applicants are eligible provided they meet the doctoral, disciplinary, regional and other programme requirements.

Can current PhD students apply?

Yes. Advanced doctoral candidates can apply if they will be able to submit official degree-conferral documentation from their university registrar by June 30, 2027.

Can someone with a PhD apply?

Yes, provided the PhD was completed within two years of the August 1, 2027 start date. For the current application cycle, the PhD must have been completed on or after August 1, 2025.

Can someone who has already completed another postdoctoral fellowship apply?

No. Individuals who hold or have completed another postdoctoral fellowship are not eligible.

Is there an age limit?

The official eligibility information focuses on the timing of PhD completion or expected completion rather than specifying a general age limit. Applicants should therefore assess eligibility primarily according to their doctoral status and completion date.

Can the fellowship be deferred?

No. The August 1, 2027 start date cannot be postponed or deferred.

Can Academy Scholars conduct research outside Cambridge?

Yes, but extensive fieldwork should generally be scheduled during winter, spring or summer breaks. Scholars are expected to remain in residence and participate in the Academy’s formal programming during the main academic period.

How many scholars are selected?

The Academy generally selects approximately five to six scholars each year, although the exact number can vary.

Conclusion

The Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027–2028 represents a highly competitive opportunity for emerging social scientists seeking dedicated time, financial support and an exceptional academic environment to advance their research.

The two-year in-residence postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University provides selected scholars with an US$80,000 annual stipend, US$6,000 in annual research support, mentorship from Senior Scholars and opportunities to participate in an interdisciplinary scholarly community.

The programme is open to applicants from all countries and citizenships, making it accessible to qualified researchers worldwide. However, applicants must meet the programme’s strict academic requirements, including having recently completed or being close to completing a PhD or equivalent degree in an eligible social science field. Their research must also demonstrate meaningful expertise in countries or regions outside the United States or Canada.

Because only a small number of Academy Scholars are selected each year, prospective applicants should invest considerable time in developing a compelling research proposal, selecting a strong scholarly writing sample, preparing an academic CV and securing high-quality recommendation letters.

For the 2027–2028 cohort, the main application deadline is September 18, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT, while recommendation letters must arrive by September 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.

Eligible researchers should begin preparing their applications well in advance and carefully review the official Harvard Academy requirements before submitting. This is particularly important for international and regional studies applicants, as the programme’s disciplinary and geographic focus is central to the selection process.

TITLE: Schuman Challenge 2027: EU-U.S. Academic Competition for Undergraduate Students

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Schuman Challenge is an annual academic competition organized by the Delegation of the European Union to the United States for undergraduate students enrolled at colleges and universities across the United States. The competition gives students the opportunity to conduct original research, develop practical policy recommendations on transatlantic issues, and present and defend their ideas before a panel of judges.

Registration for the 2027 edition is now open.

The Schuman Challenge is designed to encourage undergraduate students to engage with major issues affecting relations between the European Union and the United States. Through research, teamwork, policy analysis, public speaking and critical thinking, participants are challenged to examine a specific topic selected by the EU Delegation and develop actionable recommendations.

For students interested in international relations, political science, diplomacy, European studies, foreign policy, international security, economics, technology, public policy and transatlantic affairs, the Schuman Challenge provides an opportunity to apply academic knowledge to a real-world policy question.

About the Schuman Challenge

The Schuman Challenge is the annual foreign affairs contest organized by the European Union Delegation to the United States.

The competition focuses on EU-U.S. relations and asks participating undergraduate teams to develop policy recommendations addressing a specific topic announced by the EU Delegation.

Rather than simply writing an academic paper, participants must be prepared to present, explain and defend their recommendations before judges.

What Participants Are Expected to Do

Each participating team is expected to:

Conduct original research on the competition topic.

Examine relevant evidence and sources.

Develop actionable policy recommendations.

Prepare a 10-minute presentation.

Present the proposal to a panel of judges.

Participate in a 10-minute question-and-answer session.

Defend the team’s recommendations and respond to questions from the judges.

The competition therefore combines academic research, policy analysis, teamwork, public speaking, critical thinking and communication skills.

Schuman Challenge 2027 Registration

Registration for the 2027 edition of the Schuman Challenge is now open.

The competition is organized specifically for undergraduate students at U.S. colleges and universities. Each participating institution can enter one team consisting of three to four undergraduate students.

Prospective participants should carefully review the official registration requirements and any updated competition guidance before registering.

2027 Application Deadline

The official page provided states that registration for the 2027 edition is open, but it does not currently state a specific closing deadline.

Applicants should therefore monitor the official registration page and the EU Delegation’s Schuman Challenge webpage for updates regarding the application deadline, competition topic and detailed 2027 requirements.

How the Schuman Challenge Works

The competition is structured around several stages that give participating teams the opportunity to progress from an online preliminary round to an in-person competition in Washington, D.C.

1. University or College Registration

The Schuman Challenge operates on a university and college team basis.

Only one team from each university or college can compete.

Each team consists of three to four undergraduate students.

Students interested in participating should therefore coordinate with their institution and determine how their university or college will organize its team.

2. Preliminary Round

The preliminary round takes place online in a live format.

Participating teams present their proposals to a panel of three judges.

The preliminary rounds are held on multiple dates.

During this stage, teams are expected to demonstrate their understanding of the assigned issue, explain their recommendations clearly and respond effectively to questions from the judges.

3. Semi-Final Round in Washington, D.C.

Fifteen teams qualify from the preliminary round and are invited to participate in the semi-final stage.

The semi-final takes place in person at the EU Delegation’s office in Washington, D.C.

The selected teams present their proposals to EU officials and experts.

Semi-finalist teams receive a travel stipend and accommodation in Washington, D.C., according to the competition information.

4. Final Round

Three teams progress from the semi-final stage to the final round.

The final round also takes place in Washington, D.C.

The finalist teams present their proposals and compete for the opportunity to become the winning team of the Schuman Challenge.

The Schuman Challenge Presentation Format

Each team gives a 10-minute presentation followed by a 10-minute question-and-answer session with the judges.

Visual aids may be used during the presentation.

This means participants need to be able to communicate complex policy issues in a clear and structured manner while also responding to questions under pressure.

The presentation should demonstrate the team’s understanding of the issue, the evidence supporting its position and the practical nature of its recommendations.

Research Requirements

Participants are expected to conduct original research, cite sources and prepare policy proposals based on credible evidence.

Teams Should Be Prepared To:

Identify the central policy challenge.

Research the existing EU-U.S. relationship relating to the issue.

Examine relevant evidence and existing policies.

Identify challenges, gaps or opportunities.

Develop an actionable policy recommendation.

Support their proposal with credible sources.

Prepare a structured presentation.

Anticipate questions from the judges.

Defend their recommendations during the Q&A session.

The Winning Team’s Prize

The winning team receives a four-day Victory Tour of Brussels, the headquarters of the European Union.

During the Victory Tour, the winning students have the opportunity to visit EU institutions and engage with officials and organizations involved in European policymaking.

The winning team also has the opportunity to present its winning policy proposal to EU officials.

What the Victory Tour Can Include

The prize provides the winning students with opportunities to:

Visit European Union institutions.

Meet or engage with EU officials.

Visit relevant organizations and think tanks.

Present their winning policy proposal.

Gain exposure to European policymaking.

Learn more about EU-U.S. relations and transatlantic cooperation.

The 2026 Schuman Challenge

The 2026 edition of the Schuman Challenge took place on April 7–8, 2026, at the EU Delegation’s office in Washington, D.C.

The 2026 competition focused on the future of EU-U.S. cooperation on security.

The competition topic asked students to develop a policy proposal analyzing the current state of EU-U.S. cooperation on security and proposing an initiative or policy that could strengthen the partnership in the coming years.

2026 Competition Areas

Teams were required to consider two of four areas:

Defense

Economy, trade and energy

Technology and digital

Arctic cooperation

The topic was connected to the 250th anniversary of the signing of the U.S. Declaration of Independence and the evolution of the transatlantic relationship.

2026 Participation and Results

The 2026 edition involved universities from across the United States.

According to the EU Delegation:

34 universities participated in the preliminary rounds.

The participating universities represented 20 U.S. states and Washington, D.C.

15 teams advanced to the semi-final round.

Three teams advanced to the final round.

2026 Final Results

Macalester College, Minnesota

Patrick Henry College, Virginia

Stanford University, California

Macalester College won the 2026 competition.

The winning team developed a proposal called the “Atlantic Cable Infrastructure Program.” The proposal focused on cooperation between the European Union and United States to monitor, maintain and defend transatlantic cable systems using new technology.

The second- and third-placed teams were also commended for their policy proposals.

Skills Students Can Develop

The Schuman Challenge provides participants with an opportunity to develop practical skills that can be useful in academic, policy, diplomatic and professional environments.

Research Skills

Students conduct original research and use credible sources to support their recommendations.

Policy Analysis

Participants examine complex international issues and develop practical policy proposals.

Public Speaking

Each team must deliver a 10-minute presentation before judges.

Critical Thinking

Participants need to analyze the assigned issue and respond to questions about their recommendations.

Teamwork

Teams consist of three to four students, requiring participants to coordinate research, writing, presentation preparation and responses.

Communication

Students must explain complicated international policy issues in a clear and understandable manner.

International Affairs

The competition provides students with exposure to issues involving EU-U.S. relations, foreign affairs and transatlantic cooperation.

Who Should Consider This Opportunity?

The Schuman Challenge may be particularly relevant to undergraduate students interested in fields such as:

Political Science

International Relations

International Affairs

Diplomacy

European Studies

Foreign Policy

International Economics

Technology Policy

Public Policy

Government

International Development

Strategic Studies

However, the competition is not limited to one specific academic discipline. The key requirement is that participants meet the official eligibility requirements and can contribute effectively to their university’s team.

Important Eligibility Information

The Schuman Challenge is specifically designed for undergraduate students from U.S. colleges and universities.

Each university or college may enter only one team.

Teams consist of three to four undergraduate students.

Geographic Eligibility

The official competition description identifies undergraduate students from colleges and universities in the United States as the target participants.

Students studying at universities outside the United States should not assume that they are eligible simply because they are undergraduate students.

The competition is therefore not presented as an open worldwide opportunity for undergraduate students.

Benefits of Participating

Participating in the Schuman Challenge can provide students with several valuable experiences, including:

Opportunity to conduct original policy research.

Experience developing actionable policy recommendations.

Opportunity to present before judges and experts.

Exposure to EU officials and experts.

Experience participating in an academic foreign affairs competition.

Travel opportunity for qualifying teams to Washington, D.C.

Travel stipend and accommodation for semi-finalist teams.

Opportunity for the winning team to travel to Brussels.

Opportunity to visit EU institutions.

Opportunity to present to EU officials.

Development of teamwork and leadership skills.

Development of public speaking and presentation skills.

Exposure to transatlantic policy issues.

How to Prepare for the Schuman Challenge 2027

Students and universities interested in participating can begin preparing by taking the following steps.

Step 1: Form a Team

Identify three or four eligible undergraduate students who can work effectively together.

Step 2: Coordinate With Your University

Since only one team can represent each university or college, students should communicate with the relevant department, faculty, international affairs office or university administration about participation.

Step 3: Follow the Official 2027 Topic

The competition topic is determined by the EU Delegation. Teams should carefully study the official 2027 instructions once the topic and competition guide are available.

Step 4: Conduct Original Research

Use credible academic, governmental and institutional sources to understand the issue and the existing EU-U.S. relationship.

Step 5: Develop an Actionable Policy Proposal

Teams should develop a practical proposal rather than simply describing a problem.

Step 6: Prepare for Questions

Judges will have the opportunity to question participants, so teams should anticipate possible challenges to their recommendations.

Step 7: Practice the Presentation

The 10-minute presentation limit means teams should practice extensively to ensure that their most important arguments are presented clearly within the allotted time.

Conclusion

The Schuman Challenge 2027 is an academic competition that gives undergraduate students at U.S. colleges and universities an opportunity to engage with important issues concerning the European Union and the United States.

The competition combines original research, policy analysis, teamwork, public speaking and the development of actionable recommendations. Participants begin with an online preliminary stage, while successful teams can progress to an in-person competition in Washington, D.C.

TITLE: The Association of African Universities (AAU), in collaboration with the African Quality Assurance Network (AfriQAN) presents a Virtual workshop on Institutional Quality Assurance for Impact

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Date 29-30 April 2025 | Venue: ZOOM – http://bit.ly/4jrGnwX

Target audience

Quality Assurance Officers from universities, colleges, and other higher education institutions (HEIs), Directors/Heads of Quality Assurance Units, Higher Education Institution Leaders, National QA Agencies, Accreditation Bodies, Institutional Researchers, Monitoring & Evaluation Officers, Curriculum Developers and Academic Program Reviewers, Ministry of Education Officials / Policymakers Involved in national education policy and QA regulatory frameworks, Postgraduate Students and Researchers.

Registration link: http://bit.ly/4jrGnwX

Registration is FREE

General overview of the workshop

In an increasingly complex global landscape, there is a growing need for institutions to demonstrate their impact amid increasing worldwide demands for transparency and accountability. In higher education, Quality Assurance (QA) is essential not just for meeting standards but for driving broader outcomes like improved educational quality, institutional development, and societal progress. In sub-Saharan Africa, unique challenges and opportunities exist in aligning QA with meaningful impact. The upcoming workshop, “Institutional Quality Assurance for Impacts,” aims to provide participants with strategies, tools, and insights to strengthen QA processes and better measure, assess, and communicate institutional impacts across multiple dimensions.

Objectives

The primary objectives of the workshop are:

Enhance Understanding: To deepen participants’ understanding of institutional quality assurance and its role in driving impactful outcomes.

Tool and Strategy Development: To provide practical tools and methodologies for assessing and enhancing institutional impact through quality assurance.

Best Practices Sharing: To facilitate the exchange of best practices and experiences among institutions to strengthen quality assurance frameworks.

Action Plan Creation: To guide participants in developing actionable plans to implement or enhance quality assurance processes within their institutions for greater impact.

Workshop Structure

The workshop will be organized over two days, featuring a mix of keynote presentations, panel discussions, interactive sessions, and group activities.

Day 1: Introduction to Institutional Quality Assurance

Overview of quality assurance frameworks

The role of quality assurance in institutional effectiveness

Aligning quality assurance with institutional mission and goals

Defining and operationalizing “impact” within institutions

Day 2: Enhancing Quality Assurance for Greater Impact

Best practices in quality assurance for impact

Leveraging technology in quality assurance

Strategies for communicating impact to stakeholders

Tools and techniques for impact measurement

Methodology

The workshop will employ a mix of instructional methods to engage participants actively:

Lectures and Presentations: Delivered by experts in quality assurance and institutional development.

Interactive Discussions: Facilitated discussions to explore challenges and opportunities in institutional quality assurance.

Case Studies: Real-world examples to illustrate the successful implementation of quality assurance for impact.

Group Work and Exercises: Collaborative activities to apply learning to participants’ contexts.

Action Plan Development: Guided sessions for participants to develop tailored action plans for their institutions.

Expected Outcomes

By the end of the workshop, participants will:

Have a clear understanding of the importance of quality assurance in achieving institutional impact.

Be equipped with practical tools and methodologies to assess and enhance institutional impact.

Gain insights into best practices and successful strategies from other institutions.

Leave with a draft action plan to implement or improve quality assurance processes in their institutions.
